title: Existence of a high-value assignment for the XOR polynomial
statement:
Let $L$ be a normal form $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length $k \ge 1$ and block length $n \ge 1$, and suppose its total number of constraints is positive, $m \ge 1$. If the advantage parameter satisfies $\varepsilon \le 1/2$, then there exist a message $b : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \bbz$ and an assignment $x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \bbz$, each taking values in $\{-1, 1\}$, such that the XOR polynomial of $L$ satisfies
\[
  \psi_b(x) \;\ge\; 2\varepsilon .
\]
replaced:
Let $L$ be a normal form $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length
$k > 0$, block length $n > 0$ and at least one constraint, i.e.\ $m > 0$, and suppose the
advantage satisfies $\varepsilon \le 1/2$. Then there are a message
$b : \mathrm{Fin}\,k \to \mathbb{Z}$ and an assignment
$x : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathbb{Z}$, both taking values in $\{-1,1\}$, such that the XOR
polynomial of $L$ satisfies
\[
  \psi_b(x) \;\ge\; 2\varepsilon .
\]

\emph{Placeholder.}  The paper's Lemma 5.1 bounds the \emph{expectation}
$\E_b[\mathrm{val}(\psi_b)] \ge 2\varepsilon$; the Lean statement asserts only that \emph{some}
$b$ and $x$ achieve the bound, and is discharged by the constant all-ones witness.  The
expectation bound is \emph{not} formalised here.
